scenes.narration: My credit card has two balances. Fantastic. Even my debt has started a group chat, and neither member is explaining the assignment.
scenes.speaker: dave
scenes.visual: Two balances. One card. Keep both balance labels visibly distinct; existing character gestures only.

scenes.narration: The statement balance records what you owed when the last billing cycle ended. Think of a dated snapshot, rather than a number that follows every later purchase.
scenes.speaker: points_monk
scenes.visual: A snapshot at cycle end. Keep both balance labels visibly distinct; existing character gestures only.

scenes.narration: Here is a simplified example with no fees, interest, or other activity. A statement closes at five hundred dollars. Then a forty dollar purchase posts.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.visual: Illustrative example. Keep both balance labels visibly distinct; existing character gestures only.

scenes.narration: The current balance is now five hundred forty dollars. The issued statement still records five hundred. That newer purchase did not travel backward into the old statement.
scenes.speaker: points_monk
scenes.visual: New activity, different total. Keep both balance labels visibly distinct; existing character gestures only.

scenes.narration: So my grocery run did not invent time travel? Disappointing. I was about to demand a refund from last Tuesday and retire on the paradox.
scenes.speaker: dave
scenes.visual: No grocery time machine. Keep both balance labels visibly distinct; existing character gestures only.

scenes.narration: Continue the example: a one hundred dollar payment posts, with nothing else changing. Current balance becomes four hundred forty dollars. The original statement remains a historical record. Check the remaining amount due after payments; the old snapshot is not a second bill.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.visual: Payments change the live total. Keep both balance labels visibly distinct; existing character gestures only.

scenes.narration: Now the current number is smaller. My first plan was to pick whichever number looked friendliest. Apparently, a payment strategy needs more than excellent vibes.
scenes.speaker: dave
scenes.visual: Smaller does not explain why. Keep both balance labels visibly distinct; existing character gestures only.

scenes.narration: The closing date and payment due date are different landmarks. A grace period, when offered, sits between the billing cycle ending and the payment becoming due.
scenes.speaker: points_monk
scenes.visual: Closing date / due date. Keep both balance labels visibly distinct; existing character gestures only.

scenes.narration: The conditions matter: if your card offers a grace period and you are not carrying a balance, paying your bill in full by the due date can avoid interest on new purchases.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.visual: Keep all the conditions. Keep both balance labels visibly distinct; existing character gestures only.

scenes.narration: That is not a blanket promise about every transaction. Grace periods usually concern purchases. Cash advances generally start accruing interest immediately. Your agreement explains the terms for your card.
scenes.speaker: points_monk
scenes.visual: Not every transaction. Keep both balance labels visibly distinct; existing character gestures only.

scenes.narration: Read the statement date, payment due date, and transactions since closing together. A changed current balance describes activity; the two labels alone do not explain every charge.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.visual: Read the timeline. Keep both balance labels visibly distinct; existing character gestures only.

scenes.narration: One number is a snapshot. The other keeps updating. Great. My debt group chat finally has names, and I can stop asking a photograph for live updates.
scenes.speaker: dave
scenes.visual: Snapshot / updating total. Keep both balance labels visibly distinct; existing character gestures only.

sources.claim: Statement balance records the last cycle-end amount; later purchases and payments change current balance. Numeric examples are original illustrative arithmetic, not an account observation.
sources.excerpt: your statement balance is a record of your balance on a given date.

sources.claim: Grace periods run between cycle end and payment due date, are not mandatory, and have conditions. With a grace period and no carried balance, full on-time payment can avoid interest on new purchases. Cash advances generally accrue interest immediately.
sources.excerpt: Credit card companies are not required to give a grace period.

sources.claim: The original statement remains a cycle-end snapshot; later payments reduce current balance. Example amounts are invented arithmetic, not a real account.
sources.excerpt: But your payment should reduce your current balance.
